questions.q: Why does the summary say personality tests can be harmful?
a: They convince you that your personality cannot change
They cost too much for most people to afford
They reveal truths people would rather not hear
They reward test takers for answering dishonestly
questions.why: The overview says such tests block a growth mindset by making you think this is who you always will be.

questions.q: Which idea does Hardy list as one of the five destructive myths?
a: Your personality is inborn and fixed for life
Your goals shape the person you become
Your identity can be revised on purpose
Your habits influence how you behave
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists the belief that personality is ingrained and unchangeable among the myths he sets out to debunk.

questions.q: What does Andre Norman's story illustrate?
a: That changing your goals can change your personality
That prison makes people more determined to succeed
That childhood experiences fix who you become
That success depends mostly on meeting the right people
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Andre questioned his old goals, upgraded them, and in doing so changed his personality.

questions.q: Which three sources does Hardy suggest for finding goals that reshape identity?
a: Exposure, desire and confidence
Wealth, status and influence
Discipline, habit and willpower
Feedback, mentors and education
questions.why: Lesson 2 names exposure, desire and confidence as the places to look for the aims that drive change.

questions.q: What question pushed Nate to rethink his future?
a: What will life be like at seventy if nothing changes?
What would his parents want him to do differently?
How much weight could he lose in a single year?
Which career would pay enough to fix his health?
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes Nate picturing himself at seventy and asking whether he wanted to keep his current reality.
